builder_plan.scenario: A product assistant retrieves plausible documents but gives unsupported answers.
builder_plan.change: Change one retrieval or ranking step while keeping the document snapshot fixed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current retrieval pipeline with identical questions and answer model.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Supported answers, retrieval misses, correct abstentions, index cost, and response latency.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: When Rerankers Work Together: Better and Faster Reranking without Joint Training
summary: It replaces using a single expensive reranker (e.g., CrossEncoder, Provence, or ColBERTv2) alone by inserting a lightweight cacheable coarse scorer (Cache-Pointwise or Cache-Shapley) trained on passage relevance labels before it, optionally combined via reciprocal rank fusion. The cost is training the small scorer on relevance labels, maintaining cached representations, and added pipeline complexity, while online inference remains linear-time and pruning gets faster. Gains are not guaranteed: the paper reports that a cascade can underperform its coarse stage alone, and improvements depend on the reader model, reranker pairing, candidate budgets, and stage order, so a mismatched configuration can degrade accuracy.
rationale: The method uses small trainable scorers on top of off-the-shelf rerankers, which fits constrained infrastructure, but the paper itself shows gains vary by reader, reranker pairing, and stage configuration, so adoption requires validation on the reader's own pipeline.
technique: Training-free composition of heterogeneous rerankers with cacheable coarse scorers

claims.statement: It replaces using a single expensive reranker (e.g., CrossEncoder, Provence, or ColBERTv2) alone by inserting a lightweight cacheable coarse scorer (Cache-Pointwise or Cache-Shapley) trained on passage relevance labels before it, optionally combined via reciprocal rank fusion. The cost is training the small scorer on relevance labels, maintaining cached representations, and added pipeline complexity, while online inference remains linear-time and pruning gets faster. Gains are not guaranteed: the paper reports that a cascade can underperform its coarse stage alone, and improvements depend on the reader model, reranker pairing, candidate budgets, and stage order, so a mismatched configuration can degrade accuracy.

Inserting the lightweight cacheable scorers before CrossEncoder or Provence improves answer accuracy by 4.02-9.43 percentage points and accelerates online pruning by 1.57-1.88x; Cache-Pointwise fused with ColBERTv2 via RRF gains 4.60 points at 1.36x speedup.
